sections.h2: Who handles a Laurel County tax bill
sections.html:
Three offices in and around London split the job. Valuation sits with the PVA, payment with the sheriff, and leftovers with the clerk. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

The rate differs by taxing district, so get the figure for your own parcel from the sheriff or the PVA.

sections.h2: Laurel County housing at a glance
sections.html: London is the seat, and Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. The county had an estimated 63,746 residents in July 2025, up from 62,613 in 2020. It has 27,063 housing units and 23,996 households, and 71.6 percent are owned by their occupants. The middle home value is $159,500. Owners with a mortgage have a median monthly cost of $1,239, and owners without one pay $382. About 19.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group the homestead exemption below serves.

The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • Anyone who clears the full amount by November 1 pays 2 percent less.
  • November 2 through December 31 means paying the printed total.
  • January adds 5 percent on top.
  • From February, the add-on is 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff accepts payment three ways: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Cash does not belong in either the mail or the box, and a mailed receipt needs an envelope you have addressed and stamped.

Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. Each May the roll of real property is open for public viewing, starting on the first Monday and lasting thirteen days with Saturdays included. The clerk's office accepts the written appeal until closing time on the first workday after the viewing days end.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Useful proof includes comparable sales, an insurance policy, construction costs, or a description of the lot. Appeals that arrive without documents get denied, and a no-show at the hearing forfeits any later claim to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A bill printed before the dispute ends uses the owner's number, and the board's higher value would trigger a supplemental bill.

For 2025 and 2026 the exemption is $49,100 of assessed value. Eligible owners are at least 65 years old or classified as totally disabled. With so many older residents, a share of Laurel County sellers may have it on file already.

Applications are filed at the PVA's Room 127 office, along with documents showing age or disability. A claim based on disability is renewed yearly, except for owners with a service connected disability and owners whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has already ruled permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

sections.h2: What a delinquent bill turns into
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff's collection season ends. Open bills pass to the clerk, who files a lien and calls each a certificate of delinquency. A 1 percent monthly interest charge starts, and even a few days into a month counts as the whole month. The state's sample bill is $1,000. At the handoff it stands at $1,254 on an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, and every later step adds interest plus commissions for the clerk and county attorney.

What a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill costs the longer it sits at the clerk
Payment pointTotalGain
Handoff from sheriff$1,254.00none
Inside five business days$1,387.79$133.79
Following the first county attorney letter$1,611.30$357.30
Month two, in May$1,627.61$373.61
Once listed in the June newspaper$1,659.90$405.90
Taken over by a buyer at the sale$1,704.21$450.21

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days, and the second names the sale date. The clerk sets the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and an outside buyer of the certificate can add hefty fees of its own. Buyers register with the clerk ahead of the sale and post a deposit of 25 percent of their list value. KRS 134.015 lets that lien last eleven years, whoever holds title.

sections.h2: Tax steps to finish before listing
sections.html:
• Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • Use the bill search links on the sheriff's website to pull the parcel's tax history, and bring the printout to the listing appointment.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA what happens to it at the sale.
  • Spell out in the contract how this year's bill is divided so each side's share is clear to the closing agent.

A seller who prefers to avoid repairs can request a direct cash offer. Any balance due is deducted from the proceeds.

The tax year runs from January 1, and the bill is assessed to whoever owns the parcel on that date. If you sell in the spring, the bill that arrives in the fall may still carry your name. The closing agent normally prorates the year between you and the buyer on the settlement statement, then pays the sheriff from the proceeds.

Bring the agent the latest bill and your sheriff statement so the proration starts from real figures, not guesses. If the clerk shows a certificate against the parcel, the payoff comes out of your side of the closing before you get paid. A cash sale handles all of this the same way, but without waiting for a buyer's lender to order its own tax search.

faqs.q: Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

faqs.q: How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?
faqs.a: Two percent off the bill, if the sheriff has full payment by November 1. From the next day through December the printed amount stands.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: Start with the PVA's office at (606) 864-2889, because a meeting there is required before any appeal.

faqs.q: How much does the Kentucky homestead exemption take off?
faqs.a: Qualifying owners lose $49,100 of assessed value, and applications go to the PVA.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien under KRS 134.015 can run eleven years regardless of ownership, so a buyer's title agent looks for it.
